confidenceLevels.verified: Confirmed against shipped archives; see evidence.
confidenceLevels.documented: Stated by an upstream document; see references.
confidenceLevels.implemented: Implemented by readers in this family and self-consistent, but no shipped archive was available to confirm it.
confidenceLevels.unresolved: Not known. Recorded so it is not silently guessed at.

conventions.stringTrim: remove leading and trailing code points <= U+0020, control characters included

directoryValidation.note: POD1 carries no version marker in any available archive. Try each candidate layout in order and accept the first whose whole directory validates.

nameField.note: The path is the first NUL-terminated string. Entry lookup must use only that string.

payloads.layout: contiguous, in directory order, no alignment or padding

openQuestions.summary: Upstream notes describe production extended archives as carrying a version-tagged header. No available document gives the tag bytes, its offset, or the resulting directory origin.
openQuestions.consequence: The layout above is the untagged interpretation. A tagged archive whose directory does not begin at byte 84 will not be read.
openQuestions.action: Retain any known-good extended archive as a fixture and revise detection from observed bytes.

fields.name: unidentified3
fields.note: distinct per entry, probably a checksum

pathReconstruction.rule: if pathRemainder starts with a backslash and pathPrefix matches ^[A-Z0-9_]+$ then pathPrefix + pathRemainder; else if pathRemainder is non-empty then pathRemainder; else the whole 64-byte field as one string
pathReconstruction.note: The upper-case test distinguishes a directory prefix from payload that happens to sit in those four bytes.

nameField.postTerminatorContent: heap junk; SC24.EPD pads every record with the repeating pattern BA AD F0 0D

paletteRecord.summary: The early Terminal Reality packer wrote a second NUL-terminated string after the path on every .RAW entry: the file name of the .ACT palette the art was authored against.
paletteRecord.location: immediately after the path terminator, at len(path) + 1
acceptanceRules: the entry path ends in .RAW, case-insensitive
the second string ends in .ACT, case-insensitive
the second string is a bare file name with no directory part
paletteRecord.rejectionNote: Both rules are required. The community archive POWER.POD carries 30 second strings, 21 on non-RAW entries and none ending in .ACT, which are uninitialised buffer contents.

resolution.matchAgainst: the file name of each entry, not its full path
resolution.absentExample: MTM1 TRUCK.POD names METALCR2.ACT, which ships in GAME.POD
resolution.onAbsent: fall back to name-based palette resolution

paletteRecord.priority: authoritative; takes precedence over every name-based rule

rejectWhen.reason: guards against non-POD input; Hellbender GAME.POD has 4341 entries so a lower cap is wrong
a valid directory has no unnamed entries

rejectWhen.check: path contains a code point < 0x20 or a colon

rejectWhen.reason: cannot be terminated inside the widest field

rejectWhen.check: offset > fileSize or length > fileSize - offset
rejectWhen.reason: payload outside the file; written this way to avoid 32-bit overflow

writerRules.rule: Emit POD1 when every complete path fits in 31 bytes; emit POD1_64 only when a path needs the wider field.
writerRules.reason: extended archives are unreadable by original engines and tools

writerRules.rule: Count any directory prefix, the stem, the extension and the terminator against the budget.
A path that does not fit the widest available field is an error.
writerRules.reason: a shortened name produces an archive that mounts and then cannot find its own content

writerRules.rule: Write an entry's original name field, and the header comment field, back verbatim when they fit the layout being emitted and their string is unedited.
writerRules.reason: rebuilding a field from its string alone discards palette records and any other post-terminator content

writerRules.rule: For an entry with no original field, write the path, a terminator, and zeros.
Payload offsets follow the directory in entry order; do not carry the source archive's offsets across a rebuild.

writerRules.reason: MTM2-era tools never wrote them and no engine is known to read them

writerRules.rule: A writer's entry cap must be at least its reader's.
writerRules.reason: a tool that opens an archive it cannot save back is a defect

roundTripProperty.statement: Given an archive's entries in original order with their original comment and name fields, a conforming writer reproduces the file byte for byte.
roundTripProperty.assumption: payloads are stored contiguously in directory order, which every surveyed archive satisfies

heuristicComparison.heuristic: any .ACT in the same archive directory

notCovered: No POD1-64 archive was available; every POD1_64 claim is unverified.
No POD2 archive was available; all POD2 claims are unverified.
One EPD archive was available, so EPD rests on a single sample.

naming policy only; no binary layout
